question: The int8_direct route's slot-local full-attention prefill hard-disables AOTriton for oracle-owning layers, leaving it on the native split-K paged kernel. What does admitting AOTriton cost and buy?

protocol.harness: in-process A/B of the two prefill entry points on identical resident sessions; no server
protocol.prompt: deterministic varied prompt, numpy default_rng(20260909), token IDs in [1000, 32000)
protocol.kv: int8_per_token_head, FP32 per-token/head scales, max_sequence_length 16384 so the route is int8_direct with no BF16 mirror
protocol.oracle: packed-before vs packed-after. Packed-vs-scalar parity is NOT the oracle: the two entry points already disagree on this route by design (different GDN state-capture arithmetic, generation/qwen35_gguf.py:7406-7408).

regression_proof.claim: default OFF is bit-identical to the pre-change tree

scalar_bulk_control.note: untouched by the flag; confirms change scoping

route_context_at_8192_tok_s.note: This change closes the packed-vs-scalar half only. The residual ~6x to BF16 is the oracle route's own BF16-oracle-plus-INT8 double write and cast, not the attention kernel.

variance_note: Same-session run-to-run spread on the packed baseline is ~13% (82.71 and 93.97 tok/s across runs at 4,096), so 4,096 is 1.4-1.6x; 8,192 is the firmer point and the ratio grows with context.
blocker_to_default_on: Attention reduction order changes (logit0 delta 5.27e-3), so promotion requires the production-profile calibrated mean/tail/max KL and top-1 gate over the full mtp-bench category suite. Not run in this unit.
